title: CJP Leaders Detained Inside Plane After Landing in Delhi for Jantar Mantar Protest
excerpt: Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were taken into custody inside their Air India flight at IGI Airport; the party says the agitation will continue under Ajinkya Shinde.
body:
• Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained by Delhi Police inside their Air India aircraft moments after it landed at Delhi's IGI Airport on Saturday morning, en route from Mumbai to lead the planned Jantar Mantar protest.
  • Women police personnel boarded the plane and told the leaders the demonstration had been denied permission. Dipke challenged the officers on camera — “Come arrest us, we are not afraid” — and called the action a dictatorship, saying “even Indira Gandhi did not do this” during the Emergency.
  • The CJP condemned the move as a pre-planned interception meant to cripple the protest's leadership, handed the protest baton to organisation in-charge Ajinkya Shinde via a pre-recorded video, and insisted the agitation would continue nationwide regardless.
  • The detentions were part of a sweeping crackdown: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was picked up from his Gurugram home, CPI(M) leaders including Pinarayi Vijayan were detained at Jantar Mantar, and Delhi Police figures put the day's total detentions at around 1,000.

Delhi Police detained Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke and two top aides inside their Air India flight moments after it landed at Indira Gandhi International Airport on Saturday morning — an extraordinary interception that stopped the protest's leadership before it could reach the ground.

Dipke, co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka had flown in from Mumbai to lead the CJP's planned “Jantar Mantar 2.0” demonstration demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Police sources said multiple teams had been positioned at the airport with special access passes, and the leaders were taken to an undisclosed location within the airport premises.

“Come arrest us, we are not afraid”

Video footage circulated on social media showed women police personnel boarding the aircraft and informing the leaders that permission for the demonstration had been denied. Dipke was heard challenging the officers, asking how police could enter the aircraft and declaring that he had come prepared to be arrested.

“This is not something even Indira Gandhi did during the Emergency; this is a worse situation than that, and we are all prepared for arrest.”

— Abhijeet Dipke, CJP founder

“You could have waited till we came out. Come arrest us, we are not afraid,” Dipke told the officers, also addressing fellow passengers: “You can see where the nation is leading to.” The party's X account posted the footage, condemning what it called authoritarian detention.

Pre-planned interception, says CJP

In a statement, the CJP called the airport action “a pre-planned interception by the Delhi Police aimed at crippling the leadership of today's peaceful demonstrations before they even reach the protest site,” denouncing it as a violation of freedom of movement and demanding the immediate, unconditional release of the three leaders.

Anticipating arrest, Dipke had recorded a video the night before. “Until Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka are in detention, CJP's Organisation In Charge Ajinkya Shinde will lead this protest at Jantar Mantar,” the party said. Shinde's message to supporters, carried in live coverage: “Wherever police stop you, that's your Jantar Mantar.”

A sweeping crackdown

The airport detention was one piece of a much wider operation. YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was detained from his family residence in Gurugram's Sector 56 in a joint Delhi–Gurugram police operation. CPI(M) leaders — including Pinarayi Vijayan, M.A. Baby, Brinda Karat and John Brittas — were detained as soon as they arrived at Jantar Mantar. Tushar Gandhi, the Mahatma's great-grandson, was detained in Mumbai, and AAP leader Manish Sisodia in Chandigarh. PTI put the number detained across the New Delhi area at around 150 earlier in the day; ANI, citing Delhi Police sources, later put it near 1,000. Mobile internet was blocked within a 4-km radius of the Janpath–Kartavya Path intersection, 57 metro stations saw entry/exit curbs, and 10 temporary detention centres were set up across the capital.

Diaspora angle

For Indians abroad, the footage of police boarding a commercial aircraft to detain political leaders will be the defining image of the day — and a measure of how the state is handling dissent. The Supreme Court has listed a special Sunday sitting on petitions challenging both the transport shutdowns and the preventive detentions, so the legal verdict on Saturday's crackdown comes quickly.

What's next

With Dipke, Das and Ranka in custody at an undisclosed location and Shinde leading in their place, the CJP says the agitation continues nationwide. The immediate question is whether Sunday's Supreme Court hearing — on the contempt plea over the shutdowns and the challenge to the detentions — restrains the crackdown or endorses it.
